chunks: And in the narration of Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd: that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said to a man,

“When distress afflicts you, then wipe your hand over the place of your sajdah, then wipe your hand over your face from the side of your left cheek and over your forehead to the side of your right cheek.”
He said: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr said: In this manner Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd described it to us.
“Then say: In the Name of Allah,
‘the One besides Whom there is no god, the Knower of the unseen and the seen... the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.’
O Allah, remove from me grief and sorrow,” three times.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: beginning the supplication in the Name of Allah
key_terms.عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ: the Knower of the unseen and the seen
key_terms.هَمٌّ: distress or anxiety that afflicts a person

ai.seo_question: What should one say and do when afflicted by grief or distress according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a practical supplication for times of distress, combining a physical act connected to sajdah with invocation of Allah’s divine names and attributes. It emphasizes seeking relief from grief and sorrow through du'a and remembrance of Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.969 - In a narration from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, it is mentioned that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) advised a man:

“When you are afflicted by distress, place your hand on the spot of your prostration, then wipe your hand over your face starting from the left cheek, then over your forehead, ending at the right cheek.”
Ibn Abi Umayr stated that Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid described it to us in the same manner.
The Imam continued, “Then say: ‘In the name of Allah (swt),
the One besides whom there is no deity, the Knower of the unseen and the seen.. the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. O’ Allah (swt), remove from me distress and grief.’”
